summary: Everdell is a soft-edged worker placement and tableau builder where you gather berries, twigs, resin, and pebbles to construct a woodland city of critters and buildings over four seasons. The tension comes from a tight worker supply, timing when to pass into the next season, and chaining card discounts and card-draw engines rather than direct conflict with opponents.
praised: Stunning production values and the 3D tree tray
Satisfying engine-building as card discounts and bonuses chain together
Approachable rules for the theme and component heft, works well solo
Charming, relaxing theme that appeals beyond typical euro-gamers
criticised: Card draw luck can swing available buildings/critters significantly
Can feel solitaire-ish with limited meaningful interaction between players
Some card combos are notably stronger than others, creating balance complaints
Base game can run long for the amount of decision depth, especially at higher player counts

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking on shared locations, otherwise mostly parallel tableau building

scoring.why: Points come from building/critter values, completed events, seasonal bonuses, and end-game city/card synergies, so the winner is usually whoever assembles the most efficient multi-source scoring engine.
